page: Microsoft Azure D2lds_v5 is a low-memory, local-disk-equipped virtual machine belonging to the DLDSv5 server family. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, this instance features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with Hyper-Threading enabled. It is configured with 4.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and includes a bundled 77 GB local SSD. The underlying virtualization is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V on an x86_64 architecture.

Performance benchmarks indicate moderate single-core capabilities but limited multi-core scaling. The single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the average tier, supported by hardware features like AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration. However, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, register in the lower tenth percentile. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached read and write speeds measuring 14.8 GB/sec and 13.77 GB/sec respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2lds_v5 offers a low-cost entry point with dedicated CPU allocation, making it more predictable than shared-core burstable instances. The primary tradeoff is the highly constrained 4.0 GB memory capacity, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive applications. This server is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, small-scale text processing, or development environments that require dedicated CPU cycles but minimal memory footprints.
